paper.title_en: Reentrance of proton-neutron pairing in hot nuclear systems
paper.abstract_en: We develop a generalized finite-temperature proton-neutron BCS framework using the superoperator formalism, incorporating both isovector and isoscalar monopole pairing channels. Numerical calculations for a schematic equidistant multilevel model and realistic even-even Ge isotopes demonstrate the emergence of proton-neutron (<math><mrow><mi>p</mi><mi>n</mi></mrow></math>) pairing reentrance in even-even asymmetric (<math><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>></mo><mi>Z</mi></mrow></math>) nuclei with preexisting like-nucleon pairing correlations. This nonmonotonic behavior arises from thermal excitations that partially lift Pauli blocking of single-particle orbitals near the chemical potentials, thereby enlarging the phase space for <math><mrow><mi>p</mi><mi>n</mi></mrow></math> pair formation. We uncover a delicate interplay between thermal unblocking and like-nucleon pairing, which can either suppress or enhance <math><mrow><mi>p</mi><mi>n</mi></mrow></math> correlations depending on temperature and shell filling. A qualitative analysis of Fermi charge-exchange strength functions in hot <math><mmultiscripts><mi>Ge</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>72</mn></mmultiscripts></math>, which neglects the residual interaction between thermal quasiparticles, suggests that <math><mrow><mi>p</mi><mi>n</mi></mrow></math> pairing reentrance may alter the transition strength distribution around <math><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo>≈</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> MeV. This indicates that finite-temperature <math><mrow><mi>p</mi><mi>n</mi></mrow></math> correlations could potentially impact stellar weak-interaction rates in <math><mrow><mi>r</mi><mi>p</mi></mrow></math>-process and supernova environments.
